ja: 世界初のウェブカメラの一つは、ケンブリッジ大学の研究室で、コーヒーポットが空かどうかを見るために作られた（1991年）。
easy: One of the first webcams was used to watch a coffee pot at Cambridge University.
std: One of the first webcams was set up at Cambridge University in 1991 so researchers could check whether the coffee pot was empty.

ja: キーボードのQWERTY配列は、19世紀のタイプライターで生まれた。
easy: The QWERTY keyboard layout comes from typewriters in the 1800s.
std: The QWERTY keyboard layout originated with 19th-century typewriters.

ja: 「保存」のアイコンによく使われるフロッピーディスクは、1970年代にIBMが開発した。
easy: The 'save' icon looks like a floppy disk. Floppy disks were made in the 1970s.
std: The floppy disk, still used as the 'save' icon, was developed by IBM in the 1970s.

ja: 今のスマートフォンの計算能力は、アポロ11号の誘導コンピューターの数百万倍以上と言われる。
easy: A modern smartphone is millions of times more powerful than the Apollo 11 computer.
std: A modern smartphone has millions of times the computing power of the Apollo 11 guidance computer.

ja: 上下の向きを気にせず差せるUSB Type-Cの規格は2014年にできた。
easy: USB-C, which you can plug in either way, was created in 2014.
std: The reversible USB-C connector standard was published in 2014.

ja: 青色LEDの発明で、赤﨑勇・天野浩・中村修二の3人が2014年にノーベル物理学賞を受けた。
easy: Three Japanese-born scientists won the 2014 Nobel Prize for the blue LED.
std: Isamu Akasaki, Hiroshi Amano and Shuji Nakamura won the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics for inventing efficient blue LEDs.

ja: 日本で初めてブラウン管に「イ」の字を映したのは、1926年の高柳健次郎。
easy: In 1926, Takayanagi Kenjiro showed the Japanese letter 'イ' on an early TV screen.
std: In 1926, Kenjiro Takayanagi displayed the katakana character 'イ' on a cathode-ray tube, a milestone in Japanese television.

ja: 新幹線は1964年の開業以来、乗客が死亡する衝突・脱線事故を起こしていない。
easy: Since 1964, no passenger has died in a crash or derailment on the Shinkansen.
std: Since opening in 1964, the Shinkansen has had no passenger fatalities due to collisions or derailments.

ja: リニア中央新幹線の試験車両は、2015年に時速603kmを記録した。鉄道の世界最高速度。
easy: In 2015, a Japanese maglev train went 603 km per hour, a world record.
std: A Japanese maglev test train set the world rail speed record of 603 km/h in 2015.

ja: GPSはもともとアメリカの軍事用に作られ、1980年代以降に民間でも使えるようになった。
easy: GPS was first made for the US military. Later, everyone could use it.
std: GPS was developed by the US military and opened to civilian use from the 1980s onward.

ja: GPS衛星は、相対性理論による時間のずれを補正しないと、1日に約10kmも位置がずれてしまう。
easy: GPS must correct for Einstein's theory of time. Without this, it would be wrong by about 10 km a day.
std: GPS satellites must correct for relativistic time effects; otherwise position errors would grow by about 10 kilometers a day.

ja: 世界のインターネット通信の多くは、海底ケーブルを通っている。衛星を通る分はごく一部。
easy: Most internet data travels through cables under the sea, not by satellite.
std: The vast majority of international internet traffic travels through undersea cables rather than satellites.

ja: よく使われる弱いパスワードの上位には、毎年のように「123456」や「password」が入る。
easy: '123456' and 'password' are among the most common passwords every year. They are very weak.
std: '123456' and 'password' regularly top lists of the most common—and weakest—passwords.

ja: 世界初のカメラ付き携帯電話の一つは、2000年に日本で発売された。
easy: One of the first phones with a camera came out in Japan in 2000.
std: One of the first commercially available camera phones was released in Japan in 2000.

ja: 1997年、IBMのコンピューター「ディープ・ブルー」が、チェスの世界チャンピオンに勝った。
easy: In 1997, a computer called Deep Blue beat the world chess champion.
std: In 1997 IBM's Deep Blue defeated reigning world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a match.

ja: 2016年、囲碁のAI「アルファ碁」がトップ棋士に勝った。囲碁はチェスよりはるかに打ち方の数が多い。
easy: In 2016, an AI called AlphaGo beat a top player of the game Go.
std: In 2016 DeepMind's AlphaGo defeated top professional Lee Sedol at Go, a game with vastly more possible positions than chess.

ja: 日本の電気の周波数は、東日本が50Hz、西日本が60Hz。明治時代に輸入した発電機の違いによる。
easy: Electricity in east Japan is 50 Hz, and in west Japan it is 60 Hz.
std: Eastern Japan uses 50 Hz electricity and western Japan 60 Hz, a split dating to generators imported from Germany and the US in the Meiji era.

ja: エジソンの電球より前にも電球はあったが、エジソンは長持ちする実用的な電球と、電気を届ける仕組みを作った。
easy: Others made light bulbs before Edison, but he made one that lasted long and a system to power it.
std: Light bulbs existed before Edison, but he developed a long-lasting practical bulb and a system to distribute electricity.

ja: 世界で1日に行われるGoogle検索は、数十億回にのぼると推定されている。
easy: People search on Google billions of times every day.
std: Google handles billions of searches every day.

ja: 世界初のSMS（ショートメッセージ）は1992年に送られた「Merry Christmas」。
easy: The first text message, sent in 1992, said 'Merry Christmas'.
std: The first SMS text message, sent in 1992, read 'Merry Christmas'.

ja: サッカーのワールドカップは1930年にウルグアイで始まった。最初の優勝国も開催国のウルグアイ。
easy: The first soccer World Cup was in Uruguay in 1930. Uruguay won.
std: The first FIFA World Cup was held in Uruguay in 1930, and the host nation won.

ja: ボウリングの歴史は古く、古代エジプトの墓からピンとボールのような道具が見つかっている。
easy: Bowling is very old. Things like pins and balls were found in an ancient Egyptian grave.
std: Bowling has ancient roots: objects resembling pins and balls were found in an Egyptian grave dating back thousands of years.

ja: バドミントンの名前は、イギリスのボーフォート公の屋敷「バドミントン・ハウス」にちなむ。
easy: Badminton is named after a big house in England called Badminton House.
std: Badminton takes its name from Badminton House, the Duke of Beaufort's estate in England.

ja: カーリングのストーンの多くは、スコットランドのアルサ・クレイグ島でとれる花こう岩から作られている。
easy: Many curling stones are made from granite from a small island in Scotland.
std: Many of the world's curling stones are made from granite quarried on Ailsa Craig, an island off Scotland.

ja: ゴルフのコースが18ホールなのは、スコットランドのセント・アンドリュースが1764年に18ホールにしたことが標準になったため。
easy: Golf courses have 18 holes because St Andrews in Scotland used 18 holes in 1764.
std: Golf courses have 18 holes because the Old Course at St Andrews adopted 18 holes in 1764, which became the standard.

ja: フィギュアスケートは、冬季五輪ができる前の1908年ロンドン夏季五輪で行われた。
easy: Figure skating was in the 1908 Summer Olympics, before the Winter Olympics existed.
std: Figure skating was contested at the 1908 London Summer Olympics, before the Winter Games existed.

ja: 日本の「野球」という訳語は、1894年ごろに中馬庚が作ったとされる。
easy: The Japanese word for baseball, 'yakyu', was created in the 1890s.
std: The Japanese word yakyū for baseball is credited to Chūma Kanae, who coined it around 1894.

ja: トライアスロンのアイアンマンは、水泳3.8km、自転車180.2km、マラソン42.2kmを続けて行う。
easy: An Ironman race is a 3.8 km swim, a 180 km bike ride, and a marathon, one after another.
std: An Ironman triathlon consists of a 3.8 km swim, a 180.2 km bike ride and a 42.2 km run, back to back.

ja: ラグビーは、1823年にイギリスのラグビー校の生徒がサッカー中にボールを持って走ったのが始まりという伝説がある。
easy: A story says rugby began in 1823 when a student picked up the ball during a soccer game.
std: Legend says rugby began in 1823 when William Webb Ellis, a pupil at Rugby School, picked up the ball and ran with it.

ja: クリケットのテストマッチは、最長で5日間続く。
easy: A Test match in cricket can last up to five days.
std: A Test match in cricket can last up to five days.

ja: 自転車レースのツール・ド・フランスは1903年に始まり、約3週間で3000km以上を走る。
easy: The Tour de France bike race started in 1903. Riders go over 3,000 km in three weeks.
std: The Tour de France, first held in 1903, covers more than 3,000 kilometers over about three weeks.

ja: スキージャンプは、飛んだ距離だけでなく、空中や着地の姿勢の美しさも採点される。
easy: In ski jumping, judges score both the distance and the style.
std: Ski jumping scores combine distance with style points for flight and landing.

ja: マラソンで初めて2時間を切ったのは、2019年のエリウド・キプチョゲ（非公認の特別レース）。
easy: In 2019, Eliud Kipchoge ran a marathon in under two hours in a special race.
std: In 2019 Eliud Kipchoge became the first person to run a marathon distance in under two hours, in a specially organized event not eligible for records.

ja: マイケル・フェルプスはオリンピックで金メダル23個を獲得した。歴代最多。
easy: Michael Phelps won 23 Olympic gold medals, more than anyone else.
std: Swimmer Michael Phelps won 23 Olympic gold medals, the most of any athlete.

ja: 相撲の土俵の直径は4.55m（15尺）。
easy: A sumo ring is 4.55 meters across.
std: A sumo ring, or dohyō, is 4.55 meters in diameter.

ja: チェスの最初の4手だけでも、指し方の組み合わせは約3000億通り以上ある。
easy: After just four moves each in chess, there are hundreds of billions of possible games.
std: After just four moves by each player in chess, there are over 288 billion possible positions.

ja: スポーツクライミング、スケートボード、サーフィン、空手は、2021年の東京オリンピックで初めて採用された。
easy: Climbing, skateboarding, surfing, and karate were new sports at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.
std: Sport climbing, skateboarding, surfing and karate made their Olympic debut at the Tokyo 2020 Games, held in 2021.

ja: オリンピックの金メダルは、ほとんどが銀でできていて、表面を金でメッキしている。
easy: Olympic gold medals are mostly silver with a thin layer of gold.
std: Olympic gold medals are made mostly of silver plated with gold.

ja: 箱根駅伝は1920年に始まり、毎年1月2日・3日に東京と箱根の間を往復する。
easy: The Hakone Ekiden relay race started in 1920. It is held every January 2 and 3.
std: The Hakone Ekiden university relay began in 1920 and runs between Tokyo and Hakone every January 2 and 3.

ja: 大谷翔平は2024年、メジャーリーグで史上初めて1シーズンに本塁打50本・盗塁50個以上を達成した。
easy: In 2024, Ohtani Shohei became the first major leaguer with 50 home runs and 50 stolen bases in a season.
std: In 2024 Shohei Ohtani became the first player in Major League history to record 50 home runs and 50 stolen bases in one season.

ja: 142857に1から6までをかけると、同じ数字が順番を回したように現れる。たとえば142857×2＝285714。
easy: Multiply 142857 by 1 to 6, and the same digits appear in a new order.
std: Multiplying 142857 by any number from 1 to 6 gives a rotation of the same digits, such as 142857 × 2 = 285714.

ja: 「モンティ・ホール問題」：3つの扉から1つ選び、司会者がはずれを1つ開けたとき、別の扉に選び直すと当たる確率は2倍になる。
easy: In the Monty Hall problem, switching doors doubles your chance of winning.
std: In the Monty Hall problem, switching to the other unopened door doubles your chance of winning, from one third to two thirds.

ja: 6は、自分以外の約数（1, 2, 3）を足すと自分になる「完全数」。次の完全数は28。
easy: 6 is a 'perfect number': 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. The next one is 28.
std: Six is a perfect number, equal to the sum of its other divisors, 1, 2 and 3; the next is 28.

ja: コンパスと定規だけでは、どんな角でも3等分することはできない。1837年に証明された。
easy: With only a compass and a ruler, you cannot divide every angle into three equal parts.
std: It was proved in 1837 that a general angle cannot be trisected using only a compass and straightedge.

ja: ピタゴラスの定理（直角三角形の3辺の関係）は、ピタゴラスより1000年以上前のバビロニアでも知られていた。
easy: The Babylonians knew the Pythagorean theorem over 1,000 years before Pythagoras.
std: The relationship described by the Pythagorean theorem was known in Babylonia more than a thousand years before Pythagoras.

ja: 1729は「タクシー数」と呼ばれる。2つの立方数の和で2通りに表せる最小の数で、ラマヌジャンの逸話で有名。
easy: 1729 is called the 'taxicab number' because of a story about the mathematician Ramanujan.
std: 1729, the smallest number expressible as a sum of two cubes in two ways, is known as the taxicab number after an anecdote about Ramanujan.

ja: googol（10の100乗）という名前は、1920年代に数学者の9歳のおいが考えた。
easy: The name 'googol' for 10 to the 100th power was made up by a nine-year-old boy.
std: The name 'googol', for 10 to the 100th power, was coined by a mathematician's nine-year-old nephew.

ja: 「ハノイの塔」は、円盤を1枚ずつ動かして別の棒に移すパズル。64枚だと、最短でも約1800京回の移動が必要になる。
easy: The Tower of Hanoi puzzle with 64 disks would need more than 18 quintillion moves.
std: Solving the Tower of Hanoi with 64 disks requires 2^64 − 1 moves, more than 18 quintillion.

ja: メビウスの帯は、表と裏の区別がない面。紙の帯を半回転ねじってつなぐと作れる。
easy: A Möbius strip has only one side. You make it by twisting a paper strip once.
std: A Möbius strip, made by joining a strip of paper with a half twist, has only one side.

ja: サイコロ2個を振ったとき、出やすい合計は7。6通りの組み合わせがある。
easy: When you roll two dice, 7 is the most common total.
std: With two dice, 7 is the most likely total, since six combinations produce it.

ja: ミツバチの巣が六角形なのは、同じ材料で最も広い面積を囲めるから。数学的に証明されたのは1999年。
easy: Honeycombs are hexagons because this shape uses the least wax. This was proved in 1999.
std: Honeycomb cells are hexagonal because hexagons divide a surface with the least total perimeter, a result proved by Thomas Hales in 1999.

ja: 1メートルは、もとは北極から赤道までの距離の1000万分の1として決められた。
easy: One meter was first defined as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator.
std: The meter was originally defined as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator.

ja: 1時間が60分なのは、古代メソポタミアの60進法に由来する。
easy: An hour has 60 minutes because of an ancient counting system based on 60.
std: The 60-minute hour comes from the base-60 number system of ancient Mesopotamia.

ja: 「平均値」と「中央値」は違う。少数のお金持ちがいると平均年収は高くなるが、中央値はあまり変わらない。
easy: The average and the median are different. A few rich people raise the average a lot.
std: The mean and the median differ: a few very high incomes pull the average up but barely move the median.

ja: コインを投げて表が5回続いても、次に表が出る確率はやはり2分の1。「次こそ裏」と思うのは「ギャンブラーの誤謬」。
easy: After five heads in a row, the next coin flip is still 50/50.
std: After five heads in a row, the chance of heads on the next toss is still one half; expecting otherwise is the gambler's fallacy.

ja: 複利の「72の法則」：72を年利（％）で割ると、お金が2倍になるおよその年数がわかる。年6％なら約12年。
easy: The 'rule of 72': divide 72 by the interest rate to find how many years it takes to double your money.
std: The 'rule of 72' estimates doubling time: divide 72 by the annual percentage rate, so money at 6 percent doubles in about 12 years.

ja: ガウスは子どものころ、1から100までの合計を一瞬で5050と答えたという逸話がある。
easy: A story says young Gauss quickly found that 1 + 2 + ... + 100 = 5050.
std: According to a famous story, the young Carl Friedrich Gauss quickly summed the numbers from 1 to 100 to get 5050.

ja: 三角形の内角の和は180度だが、球面の上に描いた三角形では180度より大きくなる。
easy: The angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees, but on a ball, they add up to more.
std: A triangle's angles sum to 180 degrees on a flat surface, but to more than 180 on a sphere.

ja: 「黄金比」は約1対1.618。美しい比率と言われるが、名画や建築に使われているという話の多くは根拠が弱い。
easy: The golden ratio is about 1.618. Many stories about it in famous art are not true.
std: The golden ratio is about 1.618; many claims about its use in famous art and buildings are weakly supported.

ja: 「ベンフォードの法則」：人口や金額など身の回りの多くのデータでは、最初の数字が1である割合が約30％と最も多い。
easy: In many real lists of numbers, about 30% start with the digit 1.
std: Benford's law observes that in many real-world data sets, about 30 percent of numbers begin with the digit 1.

ja: 日本は約1万4000以上の島からなる。2023年の数え直しで、それまでの約6800から大きく増えた。
easy: Japan has over 14,000 islands. A new count in 2023 found twice as many as before.
std: A 2023 recount found Japan has over 14,000 islands, about double the long-cited figure of 6,852.

ja: 世界で最も海岸線が長い国はカナダ。
easy: Canada has the longest coastline in the world.
std: Canada has the longest coastline of any country.

ja: 中国は東西に広い国だが、全国で一つの標準時（北京時間）を使っている。
easy: China is very wide, but the whole country uses one time zone.
std: Despite spanning a wide area, China uses a single time zone, Beijing Time.

ja: モナコは世界で2番目に小さい国で、人口密度は世界最高水準。
easy: Monaco is the second smallest country, and very crowded.
std: Monaco is the world's second-smallest country and one of the most densely populated.

ja: サハラ砂漠の広さは約900万平方kmで、アメリカ合衆国や中国に近い。
easy: The Sahara Desert is about as big as the United States or China.
std: The Sahara covers about nine million square kilometers, comparable to the United States or China.

ja: カスピ海は世界最大の湖。名前に「海」とつくが、陸に囲まれているため湖に分類されることが多い。
easy: The Caspian Sea is the biggest lake in the world.
std: The Caspian Sea, despite its name, is usually classed as the world's largest lake.

ja: ロシアのバイカル湖は世界で最も深い湖で、世界の湖や川の淡水（凍っていないもの）の約2割をたたえている。
easy: Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake. It holds about 20% of the world's fresh surface water.
std: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world and holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water.

ja: ネパールの国旗は、四角形でない唯一の国旗。2つの三角形を重ねた形をしている。
easy: Nepal's flag is the only national flag that is not a rectangle.
std: Nepal has the only non-rectangular national flag, formed of two stacked triangles.

ja: グリーンランドは地図では大きく見えるが、実際の面積はアフリカの約14分の1。
easy: Greenland looks huge on maps, but Africa is about 14 times bigger.
std: Greenland looks enormous on Mercator maps, but Africa is actually about 14 times larger.

ja: 世界で最も雨が多い場所の一つは、インドのメガラヤ州。年間降水量が1万mmを超える年もある。
easy: One of the rainiest places in the world is in India. It can get over 10 meters of rain a year.
std: Parts of India's Meghalaya state are among the wettest places on Earth, with annual rainfall that can exceed 10,000 millimeters.

ja: チリのアタカマ砂漠は、極地を除いて世界で最も乾燥した場所の一つ。何年も雨が降らない観測所もある。
easy: The Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places. Some places get no rain for years.
std: Chile's Atacama Desert is one of the driest non-polar places on Earth; some weather stations have recorded no rain for years.

ja: ノルウェーのフィヨルドは、氷河が削った深い谷に海水が入りこんでできた。
easy: Norway's fjords were made by glaciers cutting deep valleys that filled with seawater.
std: Norway's fjords are deep valleys carved by glaciers and later flooded by the sea.

ja: 日本の国土の約3分の2は森林。先進国の中でも森林の割合が特に高い。
easy: About two-thirds of Japan is covered by forest.
std: About two-thirds of Japan is forested, one of the highest shares among developed countries.

ja: 日本には活火山が111ある。世界の活火山の約7％が日本にある。
easy: Japan has 111 active volcanoes, about 7% of the world's total.
std: Japan has 111 active volcanoes, roughly 7 percent of the world's total.

ja: 赤道上の国エクアドルの国名は、スペイン語で「赤道」という意味。
easy: The name 'Ecuador' means 'equator' in Spanish.
std: Ecuador's name is simply the Spanish word for 'equator', which crosses the country.

ja: オーストラリアの首都はシドニーでもメルボルンでもなく、キャンベラ。2つの都市の争いを避けるために新しく作られた。
easy: The capital of Australia is Canberra, not Sydney or Melbourne.
std: Australia's capital is Canberra, a planned city built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

ja: ブラジルの首都ブラジリアは、1960年に内陸に新しく作られた計画都市。上から見ると飛行機のような形をしている。
easy: Brazil's capital, Brasília, was built in 1960. From above, it looks like an airplane.
std: Brasília, Brazil's capital since 1960, is a planned city whose layout resembles an airplane from above.

ja: ナイアガラの滝は、アメリカとカナダの国境にある。
easy: Niagara Falls is on the border between the US and Canada.
std: Niagara Falls sits on the border between the United States and Canada.

ja: 世界最大の滝は、海の中にあるデンマーク海峡の海底の滝。冷たい海水が約3500m落ち込んでいる。
easy: The biggest waterfall in the world is under the ocean, between Greenland and Iceland.
std: The world's largest waterfall is the underwater Denmark Strait cataract, where cold water plunges about 3,500 meters.

ja: 日本の都道府県で面積が最も小さいのは香川県。
easy: Kagawa is the smallest prefecture in Japan.
std: Kagawa is Japan's smallest prefecture by area.
